subject: Cognitive Science
title: Mental Set and Fixation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mental Set and Fixation.

hook.text: You solve ten problems the same way. Problem eleven needs a different method—but you keep using the old one.

buildup.text: A mental set is a tendency to approach problems using strategies that worked before, even when they don't fit.

discovery.text: Luchins' water jug experiments showed people missed a simple solution after practicing a complex one.

twist.text: Experience is a double-edged sword: it builds expertise and creates fixation in the same stroke.

climax.text: Breaking a mental set often requires stepping away, changing context, or asking someone with fresh eyes.

punchline.text: What worked before can block what works now.

quiz.question: What is a mental set?
options: A tendency to reuse previously successful strategies
